annotations.text: POST-MVP — rounds drawn before their slice is the work. The four canonical canvases and designs/canonical are the MVP baseline implementation reads from; this tree is where a later round is drawn, reviewed and held until its slice becomes current, at which point its boards move across to canonical as a reviewed round. Same design system, same flow grammar, same build: boards render from design/components, the page opens with a generated flow map, and graph.json binds each orange number to its outcomes. Nothing implementation needs is ever only here.

CHANGE HISTORIES — would-like #2, drawn 2026-09-22. Two kinds of history, one door rule. A post, a comment and a profile each open a chronicle: every version WHOLE, newest first, the current one marked, never a diff — the store keeps complete states, and on L1 every edit signs a full new record of its own. A removed version keeps its row and wears the mark. A stance is a history too: the bundle IS the list of records ever cast from one node to another, and the timeline says in plain words what the standing adds up to, because a sum that clips hides the conviction behind it. The doors follow one law — authoring doors are faces and fields, HISTORY DOORS ARE READOUTS: the stance face on a card is untouched, the value at a row's end opens the timeline, and the pad's Current opinion line carries the only new ink. Timelines are public to everyone, signed out included; the gates stay on acting.

CHATS — would-like #3, drawn and revised 2026-09-23. The one surface where CoGra takes messenger convention whole: a list of your chats with a floating New chat (the product's first FAB), bubbles with your own on the right, a live field at the foot. Underneath, a chat is the proposal primitive in messenger clothes — nothing here may look like a proposal. The send arrow IS the seal: tapping it signs the message in your name, and holding it opens what you sign. Each message is plaintext or encrypted by the lock beside the field — plaintext by default, sticky per chat, the state shown by the lock's fill — and every encrypted message wears a quiet lock; previews and bubbles show the words wherever you hold the key. Rows keep the ages ladder, the thread prints the clock and divides the days. The page has two faces that swap both ways: your chats, and all chats — the ordinary rank narrowed to chats, no second algorithm, your own chats hidden by default. Long-press is the second gesture: a row for the chat's options, a bubble for the message's acts. Messages never edit. The chat's detail surface, behind the thread's header, is drawn in the rows below.

CHAT DETAILS — round B1 of the chats work, drawn 2026-09-23. What the thread's header and the row menu open: a messenger's group info through CoGra's grammar. The chat's face, name and words at the top, and its own OPINION control leading the actions row (the profile header's precedent), with Edit chat beside it wherever the governance map lets the reader propose a change. Media, then OPEN DECISIONS — where an act that needs more voices than its actor's waits; empty here, filled in round B2. Search rides the thread's header, beside the details door, on every thread. The members wear their roles, and for a member each role word is a door to the role change; a Collective can be a member; an invited person who has not joined yet is marked, and NO ROW EVER SHOWS PRESENCE. Mute silences push only and lives here and on the row menu. Leave is unilateral, with an optional parting reason that stands in the chat's history. The metadata grows in whole versions like a post's — its successions — and the edit history shows them newest first with who joined, left and was invited between them, never inside them, and every member may start a version's removal — a chat has no author. The edit's seal counts three things signed together: the change, its link to the chat, and the proposer's own opinion for it. Chats are public, so a reader outside gets the same page minus the member's acts, with the join on the actions row. The multi-voice faces behind Add people, the role change, a version's removal and the change that waits for more voices are the governance rows below.

CHATS GOVERNANCE — round B2 of the chats work, drawn 2026-09-23. The multi-voice acts, in messenger clothes: nothing here may look like a proposal. An act the actor's own say settles is INSTANT — a seal counting three things signed together, the change, its link and their own opinion for it. An act that needs more voices becomes a QUIET CARD IN THE THREAD at the moment it was proposed: a plain sentence, an Agree that is the reader's voice, and a count of PEOPLE — 2 of 5 so far — that settles into one outcome line when enough agree. The same decisions stand as rows under Open decisions on the details. THE COUNT CONVENTION, for review: cards count people and never show weight; the tally underneath is weighted by role, so a card can settle early, and geek mode paints the arithmetic. Nothing expires. Inviting is the inviter's own act, never a decision: a picker, then a seal counting one invitation per person. Joining is always the joiner's own record, one seal for three routes — open, invited, approved. A request shows as a card the approver meets in the thread, with Approve. Role words open a sheet of the three roles; a version's removal is the chat's decision, and a removed version keeps its row under the chat's own mark.
